To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the complex network of interspecific interactions in a well mixed system leads to diversification rather than the optimisation of species in the environment.
the complex interactions between organisms can lead to the diversification of the community.
diversity in a biological system arises from a network of interactions between organisms, and is a consequence of this network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the emergence of diversity in biological systems.
the evolution of diversity in biological communities, and the role of interactions between species in the maintenance of diversity.
the role of interactions between species in shaping the diversity of a community.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a well-mixed biological system, such as a petri dish, can be considered a complex network of interactions, which can be considered as a co-evolutionary niche.
the interaction network is the product of diversification and not optimisation, which is the opposite of what is normally assumed.
diversity can be considered as a by-product of the interactions between organisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a complex network of interactions can lead to the co-existence of many species, which would not have survived if each had to compete alone.
a system of highly interacting organisms can diversify into many co-evolution niches, rather than optimising for one niche.
in a complex networked system, diversity is the product of the network of interactions rather than the product of the system environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

diversity is not a product of the individual, but of the interactions between individuals, and this diversity is not necessarily an optimisation of the individual, as it can be the product of co-evolutionary interactions.
the interactions formed by species in an environment may be as important as the environment itself in determining the diversity of species present.
diversity can be a product of interspecies interactions, and that the interactions between species may be more important than the species themselves.
